title: Trumpeters with harmonic sophistication
summary: He names Eldridge, Joe Newman, Dizzy, Hot Lips Page (the preacher on a recording), Buck Clayton, Shavers and Red Allen.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Of the trumpet players that you played with, who did you find to be harmonically the most interesting? I mean, if we -- we talked about the fact that you found Art Tatum an incredible harmonic challenge.
With his harmonies and his modulations and Don Byas.
Now, can you think of a trumpet -- anybody who played the trumpet who had a comparable or similar kind of harmonic sophistication?

Oh, yes, if I can think about a few whom I remember. First of all, Roy Eldridge, then Joe Newman and -- oh, my goodness, let me think. I made a recording or two with a trumpet player, forget his name offhand. Name a couple that you remember.
But this other one I'm thinking of, he
His name. I'm trying to think of his name.
Let me turn the tape recorder off, maybe we can get together.

Well, now we have discovered that the mystery trumpet player who reminds you of a kind of preacher that's in that thing, "Nothing Can Steal Your Girl Like a Fast-Talking Chicken-Eating Preacher" is none other than --
Right. 'That was Hot Lips Page, if I remember right now, yes.
Okay. Now, you said who else?
Red Allen, yes. Oh, my goodness.
